svg.title: Product defaults set the floor; configuration adds layers
svg.desc: Layered diagram of how a working footprint is built. At the bottom is the baseline harness floor: system instructions plus native tools, about 14.9k tokens for Copilot CLI, 27.2k for Claude CLI, and 20.6k for Copilot in VS Code. Configuration adds layers on top: repository instructions, skills, memory, MCP tool schemas, and finally conversation history that grows during the task. None of the baselines here had repository instructions, memory, or MCP active. The point is to avoid attributing configuration growth to the product: defaults set the floor, while repository and user configuration add the layers above it.
svg.text: The working footprint is a floor plus configuration
Each layer is measured separately so configuration growth is not mistaken for a product default.
grows as the agent reads files and calls tools
off in these baselines; can dominate when on (VS Code +39 tools → 46.4k)
none active in baseline (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / project memory)
Copilot CLI 0 on demand · Claude CLI ~1,094 catalog · VS Code ~37 folded
none active in baseline — added per repo on top of the floor
Baseline captures here had no repository instructions, memory, or MCP active by design — those are layers added on top of the floor, not part of it.
